channel.description: An education daily: policy, vocational training, classroom technology and the business of learning.

item.title: Education Daily · November 22, 2026
item.description: Six stories today sit on three ledgers: the stock of affordable preschool places, the integrity of a published notice, and the contracts between schools and companies. On November 20 Fujian's provincial legislature reviewed the government's preschool report: 6,470 kindergartens, 1.015 million children enrolled, a three-year enrolment rate of 99.52%, 95.19% of places counted as affordable, and 67.92% of children in public kindergartens against a national average of 59.4%. Thirty-eight counties have passed national universal-preschool review, the province has added 28,000 kindergarten teachers since 2021, and per-child operating funding stands at RMB 600 a year. On November 21 Chang'an University explained how a recruitment notice came to be dated a day before the interview it reported: a list image was pasted into a draft created the previous day and the publication date was never reset. Three officials were disciplined. Shenyang's Tiexi district named two illegal tutoring operations, one an unlicensed individual class and one a childcare company teaching academic subjects under a childcare licence. Zhengzhou University opened a technology business school jointly run with the provincial education, science and state-asset departments. Fujian Open University launched a battery-sector college with a company and a technician institute. And Harbin University of Science and Technology signed with Alibaba Cloud to become northeast China's first "AI beacon campus". A coverage rate is a stock, a publication date is a process, a partnership is a flow; only the three together show where the system is putting its weight. Fujian's preschool report: 6,470 kindergartens, 1.015 million children, 95.19% affordable coverage

item.title: Education Daily · November 21, 2026
item.description: Six stories today move through four ledgers: aid, degrees, skills and tools. On November 20 China Development Bank said it had finished its part of the 2026 national student loan programme, paying RMB 116.3 billion to 7.53 million students from low-income families; lifetime lending now stands at RMB 676.8 billion across 71.25 million cases. The same day Hainan's degree committee published its 2026 review: three institutions and nine programmes get new bachelor's-degree authority, and twelve more programmes cleared their own institutional review. Hubei opened its third provincial skills competition in Wuhan with 64 events and 100 workers honoured, RMB 8.4 million in prizes between them. Yunnan named five micro-major cases under the education ministry's Double Thousand programme, from carbon accounting to low-altitude aviation. Tencent's WorkBuddy education edition reported about 660,000 users after a month, with lightweight models taking 73.1% of a single day's tokens. And Kaiwen Education will put RMB 3 million into a Xiongan subsidiary to run its Zhiqi app. Money, quotas, credentials, tools: how each is allocated decides who counts as covered this year. China Development Bank finishes 2026 student loans: 7.53 million borrowers, RMB 116.3 billion

item.title: Education Daily · November 20, 2026
item.description: Six stories today sit on three tables: jobs, curriculum and budget. On November 19 the secretariat of the Central Leading Group on Education Work, together with the education, human resources, industry and state-asset authorities, projected 12.99 million graduates for 2027 — 290,000 more than the 12.70 million expected for 2026 — and set out five lines of work. The same day the education ministry published its lottery-funded study-travel list: 41 camps, 20 bases and 20 provincial red-heritage projects. Guangdong reported 168 industry-education skill chains, more than 1,100 employers and 690,000 workers trained. A national equipment-manufacturing skills contest opened in Tianjin with teams from 17 provinces and three countries. The education ministry opened a second round of discipline-specific large models, with domestic base models, 100 concurrent users and local filing before launch. And Youdao posted RMB 1.43 billion in quarterly revenue with a ninth straight profitable quarter. The numbers move in both directions; the question is who pays next year's bill. China expects 12.99 million graduates in 2027 as five central bodies set out a five-part jobs plan

item.title: Education Daily · November 19, 2026
item.description: Seven stories today land on four tables: a degree table, a subsidy table, a vacancy table and a purchase order. Tianjin University has won approval for three "PhD plus master's" dual-degree projects, about five doctoral students each, chosen through an internal second round; Fudan had already piloted the model across 10 strong disciplines with a first cohort of 10. Jilin has released RMB 58.9 million in central funding for weak links in compulsory education, with a negative list that rules out staff pay, budget balancing, debt service and outbound investment. A Guangdong recruitment tour of three Hunan campuses listed 20,458 posts, drew nearly 20,000 visitors and collected 9,930 CVs. Liaoning has published a draft list of provincial industry-education projects, open to comment for seven days. A county high school in Inner Mongolia is spending RMB 8.13 million on a "smart campus", of which items explicitly labelled AI account for about RMB 2.19 million. The Chinese Academy of Educational Sciences has launched "Jiaozhi No.1", an education-research agent, before nearly 300 attendees. And Xueda Education is putting RMB 50 million into Open Source China for a 1.23% stake. A degree, a subsidy, a vacancy, a device: in the end they all land on the same budget line. Tianjin University wins three "PhD plus master's" dual degrees: about five students each, picked internally

item.title: Education Daily · November 18, 2026
item.description: Three of today's six stories rewrite a rule; the other three rewrite a ledger. A federal judge in Massachusetts has vacated in its entirety the Homeland Security rule that would have ended Duration of Status, finding it "arbitrary, capricious and otherwise not in accordance with law": the four-year cap for F-1 and J-1 holders, the 240-day limit for I-visa media staff and the bans on transfer or a second degree do not take effect, and an appeal is expected. The education ministry has published 12 original textbooks written by nine universities, with philosophy and sport science joining the series for the first time, including three separate Introduction to Philosophy volumes. The autumn job-fair campaign has held more than 10,000 fairs since September 20, with 264,000 employers offering 5.515 million posts to 5.291 million graduate visits. Zhejiang has approved two Sino-foreign vocational colleges with six programmes and 1,410 places between them. Hong Kong Baptist University has launched AITA, a course-aware AI tutor used in more than 100 courses by over 3,000 people. And Wisdom Education expects RMB 15.6 million in net profit for FY2026, against RMB 38.3 million. Loosen a rule and the bill, and the timesheet, come into view. A federal judge vacates the fixed-term visa rule outright: D/S survives, and transfer or a second degree is no longer barred

item.title: Education Daily · November 17, 2026
item.description: Six stories about turning good intentions into something an inspector can count. The health commission, the education ministry, the traditional medicine administration and the disease control administration now require every school and kindergarten to appoint a health vice-principal, dispatched by a medical institution at mid-level title or above, with no office hours and no addition to the school's establishment, and at least four site visits and two health talks a term. Henan has published 2,359 provincial model lessons, 140 of them in AI education and all of them in primary or middle school: senior secondary gets none. The Beijing Accord, the first international vocational standard China has led, is out in six languages after consultation with more than 70 countries and release by 45, backed by memoranda with 15 national authorities. A smart irrigation consortium met in Changji with 124 institutions and firms from 20 provinces. The Fuguang Plan reached Hebei, its third province, with 268 participants, nine workshops and 50 days. And the Institute of International Education reports a 9% autumn fall in US enrolment, with 254,000 Chinese students and a sixth straight decline, as a $70,000 OPT fee is proposed. Write the standard precisely and the bill shows up. Every school and kindergarten gets a health vice-principal: no office hours, no new post, four visits a term minimum

item.title: Education Daily · November 16, 2026
item.description: Six stories about who does the gatekeeping, and who pays for it. Henan has taken public school canteens back from contractors: 12,000 schools now buy through one city platform, ingredient costs are down 31.5%, and meal fees at more than 16,000 schools sit under unified supervision. An HSK pre-university alliance will split the language barrier and the subject barrier between two countries, half a year each. A man who came first in Korea's tax accountant exam has admitted using a hidden camera and AI, and the Blue House met the same night, six days before the national college test. A business-intelligence consortium opened in Jinan with UFIDA, Central University of Finance and Economics and Shandong Vocational University of Commerce at the helm, and 378 founding members. Kunshan has switched on an AI assistant account for all 27,000 of its teachers, no application required. And the Ai Zhongwen community has launched a partner programme with more than 500 institutions on board and 32 cases chosen from 269 submissions. Change the gatekeeper and the ledger changes with it. Henan takes public school canteens back in-house: 12,000 schools on one buying platform, ingredient costs down 31.5%

item.title: Education Daily · November 15, 2026
item.description: Seven stories about one ledger: who pays for places, class hours and equipment, and who gets them. The education ministry has put 3.47 million candidates into the 2027 postgraduate exam on December 19 and 20, with question security and exam-hall screening briefed separately. The 2026 World Chinese Language Conference opened the same day with 210 million learners abroad and HSK past a million candidates a year. Jiangsu issued ten prohibitions before its first autumn holiday, including a two-week exam ban afterwards. Xicheng in Beijing wants a specialist science adviser in every school within three years. Hong Kong PolyU has folded four aerospace centres into one institute, with HK$4.3 billion of research spending behind it. Dong Mingzhu has defended Gree's technical school: 100 million yuan a year, 300 places, more than 8,000 applicants. And Pengzhou has bought an AI classroom for 6.13 million yuan, with training at 2% of the contract. Places, class hours and budgets are being rewritten at the same time. 3.47 million sign up for China's 2027 postgraduate exam, sat on December 19 and 20

item.title: Education Daily · November 13, 2026
item.description: Five stories today circle one question: what makes a credential count? China's human resources ministry has published a draft regulation on skills assessment - seven chapters, 63 articles, eight grade levels, with comment closing on December 12. In Wuhan a vice-minister sorted universities into research, applied and skills-oriented tracks while 16 school-enterprise deals were signed. Guangdong has 596 vocational schools and more than three million students, and is still working out whether they fit the factories. In Guizhou an eight-year-old was beaten with a ruler and the county conceded the punishment went too far. A Kuaishou charity, meanwhile, has packaged 30 AI classroom cases from rural schools. Certificates, categories and casebooks are all being rewritten at once. China consults on a skills-evaluation regulation: seven chapters, 63 articles and eight grade levels

item.title: Education Daily · November 12, 2026
item.description: Three stories today ask the same question from opposite ends: what makes a credential count? Seven ministries have moved engineers' continuing-education hours into a national registry and tied them to promotion. England's regulator says unsupervised assignments can no longer show what a student has learned, and wants more closed-book and oral assessment instead. Yunnan has rebuilt its vocational skills contest around 42 industry tracks, replacing the exam hall with a competition floor. Credits, hours and skill grades are being redefined at the same time. Seven ministries set continuing-education rules for engineers: six chapters, 29 articles, hours valid nationwide from January 1, 2027

item.title: Education Daily · November 11, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is that school places must follow the children. The NDRC is moving the basis for allocating places from household registration to the resident school-age population: kindergartens and compulsory schooling have peaked, vacated buildings are to be repurposed, and senior-high and higher education still need to expand. The skills side offers a different table: the national contest adds AI trainer and connected-vehicle trades, and a top-20 finish now buys a higher skill grade. Places are being reallocated while the skill standard is being redrawn. NDRC: school-age numbers have peaked for kindergartens and compulsory schooling, and senior-high places must follow the children

item.title: Education Daily · November 10, 2026
item.description: Today's thread: who gets the places, and who can prove it. Three ministries have turned the rural and poor-county admissions programme into a rural-revitalisation track covering 160 national and 390 provincial priority counties, and swapped a rural household registration for three years of actual study at a county high school. It starts with the 2030 intake. One year into the school science-education plan, the countable stock is 134 pilot districts, 1,246 pilot schools and more than 3,000 platform resources. Zhejiang's autumn job fair links 29,000 posts. Every policy ends up as a list someone has to verify. Rural-revitalisation admissions track confirmed: 160 national plus 390 provincial counties, applied from 2030

item.title: Education Daily · November 9, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is that places, jobs and courses all have to follow structural change. Yiwu is absorbing demographic waves with tidal schools: 7,650 places added and 14 more schools planned in five years. Hebei has put AI one-person companies into its graduate start-up support, while Hubei University of Automotive Technology has welded 58 undergraduate programmes to the car chain, with a 95% industry-match rate. The hard part for a school is not launching a new programme but letting old capacity, staffing and courses follow the students. Yiwu's tidal schools absorb enrolment waves: 7,650 places added, 14 more schools in five years

item.title: Education Daily · November 8, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is what time school starts, and who gets to teach. Cities are pushing arrival times back: Jiangyin primary schools at 8:00, middle schools at 7:40 and high schools at 7:20; a Chengdu primary moved to 8:40 from the start of winter; younger pupils at a Chongqing school arrive at 9:00, with first period at 9:45. On the same day, the NPC Standing Committee's vocational education law inspection team discussed its report, and the 2026 US-China Education Summit at Columbia put AI education and people-to-people exchange at the centre. A timetable is one notice; sleep, commuting and after-school care are what hold it up. Schools push back arrival and scrap morning reading: Jiangyin high schools at 7:20, a Chengdu primary at 8:40, Chongqing's youngest at 9:45 for first period

item.title: Education Daily · November 7, 2026
item.description: The thread today is who may teach and who gets a seat. The University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences opened the country's first college for endangered disciplines — bachelor's to PhD, two supervisors — and gathered more than 80 institutions into an alliance. Shandong put forward six names for national school-aesthetics teacher studios, four of them from primary and secondary schools. The University of Science and Technology Beijing's Tianjin College signed up more than 20 companies for an AI industry-education alliance. Nameplates are cheap; posts, quotas and teaching hours are what someone pays for. UCASS opens the first college for endangered disciplines, with 80-plus institutions in its alliance

item.title: Education Daily · November 6, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is gatekeeping and who pays. Sichuan split supplementary materials into review, selection and purchase-on-behalf, effective December 5, with one set per subject and a six-month gate for out-of-catalogue items. Beijing set September 1, 2027 as the deadline to end delivered meals, convert all canteens to self-operation and build 1,000 smart canteens. The same week, Beijing released an AI-in-education package; its Zhi Xiaoyan platform is already in more than 100 schools with 30,000 users. Every gate ends with someone paying. Sichuan issues school-supplement rules: one set per subject, effective December 5

item.title: Education Daily · November 5, 2026
item.description: The word today is entry points. The education ministry took the four commonest gaokao registration scams apart one by one and repeated that registration, review, payment and eligibility run through a single provincial channel. In Hong Kong, 49 university presidents spent a day on what universities owe AI, society and civilisation, and 12 institutions signed agreements. Canada's teachers' federation drew four lines around AI in schools, and Guangxi used 33 skills events to photograph what employers now want. Fewer doors means fewer middlemen. Ministry warns 2027 gaokao applicants: four scam types, one official channel

item.title: Education Daily · November 4, 2026
item.description: The word of the day is eligibility. Jiangsu published the institutions and majors it proposes to authorise for bachelor's degrees — three institutions, 17 majors, 12 of them at two vocational universities. Yunnan proposed 20 pilot counties, 60 training bases and 600 priority schools for school football, basketball and volleyball, spread across 15 prefectures. On the employment side, the education ministry's regional tour closed in Changsha with 7,100 jobs and 1,623 first-round intentions from 5,000 graduates, while a Geely dual-study cohort in Ningbo has 97% of its first graduates already interning on the line. And in Haidian, a district-run agent platform now reaches more than 80 schools, 3,000 agents and 150,000 teachers and students. Eligibility decides who gets a seat; cost decides who keeps it. Jiangsu proposes three new degree-granting institutions and 17 majors, most of them vocational

item.title: Education Daily · November 3, 2026
item.description: Every education story today points the same way: how AI gets into the classroom. The Ministry of Education’s Fujiang programme opened in Guangxi — 14 cities, 20 counties, 60 schools — on the same day it ordered nationwide AI training for teachers; 81% say AI saves them preparation time, while the harder barrier turns out to be confidence, not skill. More than 700 companies brought "AI leads the way" as the theme to the national equipment fair. And 15 listed education companies reported 18.775 billion yuan of nine-month revenue — after two years of AI talk, delivery is starting to appear in the accounts. The threshold was never the hardware. Ministry of Education’s Fujiang programme launches in Guangxi: 14 cities, 20 counties, 60 schools
